title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Routine follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient presents for routine follow-up. He manages his type 2 diabetes mellitus with both insulin and metformin. He reports adherence to his current regimen. Examination of the renal status reveals a diagnosis of CKD stage 4. I reviewed the workup and confirmed that the current CKD stage 4 is unrelated to diabetes.

Medication List
Insulin, Metformin.

Exam
Vitals are stable. Cardiovascular and pulmonary exams are unremarkable. Physical examination reveals no acute findings.

Assessment
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Management continues with insulin and oral hypoglycemic agent.
2. CKD Stage 4: Condition is assessed as being unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current regimen of insulin and metformin for type 2 diabetes. Monitor renal function closely for CKD stage 4. Follow up as scheduled.
explanations: The provider states the CKD is not due to diabetes, so the presumed link does not apply: code diabetes without complications and CKD separately.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: The 'with' presumption is overridden when the provider documents another cause or no link.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
